prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "Apply linux system expertise to this task". The fixture includes partial failure, cancellation, retry/idempotency pressure, concurrency, and an attractive topology assumption that is not established by evidence. The acceptance boundary is linux-systems: Resolve distribution, kernel, init system, architecture, cgroups, filesystem, user/namespace, and packaging context first. The adjacent bun-deno-runtime discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

requirements: service account, filesystem permission and dependency/ordering state
journal/process/cgroup evidence plus restart and clean-boot fixtures
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual linux-systems boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=backend-engineering; near-neighbor=bun-deno-runtime), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Resolve distribution, kernel, init system, architecture, cgroups, filesystem, user/namespace, and packaging context first.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.
Reproduce with read-only diagnostics first, then verify service lifecycle, permissions, resource limits, reboot/restart persistence, logs, and exact unit/package configuration after changes.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not disable security controls globally, chmod 777 broad paths, edit generated system files without ownership context, or assume commands/options are portable across distributions.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Distribution/kernel/architecture/init/cgroup/namespace and effective service/config identity; Process ancestry, credentials/capabilities, /proc descriptors/state, mount/filesystem and permission evidence; Systemd logs/unit/drop-ins, resource-limit/cgroup events and exact failure/recovery evidence; Restart/reboot persistence plus least-scoped configuration and rollback artifacts), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
